en.1: Starting today, we're finally beginning Harry Potter together.
en.4: Let's look at the cover first, shall we?
en.5: The American edition says Sorcerer's Stone, but the British edition has Philosopher's Stone.
en.6: Uh, why is the title different?
en.7: You might be wondering that — but it's not a different book.
en.8: The publisher just tweaked the one word a bit, to give kids more of a 'sorcerer' feel.
en.10: Okay, let's look at the first sentence.
en.11: The Dursleys say they're perfectly normal — and quite proudly, too.
en.12: But that's a bit strange, isn't it?
en.13: Why brag about being normal like this?
en.14: Just put a question mark right here and move on.
en.15: Actually, it's because they have something to hide — saying we're normal is them building a wall.
en.16: There's a part I really love.
en.17: It's the scene where they sit the crying kid down in a chair — and the author doesn't just write that they sat him down.
en.18: She writes wrestle — like they were wrestling with him, struggling to get him into the chair.
en.19: Just by changing one word, you can picture the kid thrashing around and the parents' flustered faces, right?
en.20: This is the joy of reading in the original language.
en.21: You skip the whole step of translating into Korean, and just feel the motion packed into the word, like a picture.
en.22: And come to think of it, Mr. Dursley — who sees a cat reading a map and just brushes it off as a trick of the light — looks a little different too, doesn't he.
en.23: In this man's world, the word 'magic' doesn't even exist, so he has no container to hold the truth right in front of him.
en.24: The world you can see grows exactly as wide as the words you know.
en.26: "Mr. and Mrs. Dursley, of number four, Privet Drive, were proud to say that they were perfectly normal, thank you very much." The Dursleys of number four, Privet Drive, were proud that they were perfectly normal.
en.27: Nobody even asked, but they were oh-so grateful to say so.
en.31: Something strange is just about to happen — but yes, even though you're curious, let's hold off for today.
en.32: Some of you have been reading for three years, some of you are here for the first time, and some of you stopped and came back — you're all here.
en.34: Just reading this one sentence out loud makes today a success.
en.35: Day by day, these add up, and before you know it, you'll have finished this whole book.
en.37: This was Stella, see you again tomorrow.
